subject: Edgebound private VPC: controlplane/dataplane split + tenant ingress review (Nimbl)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@nimblhealth.com>, infra@nimblhealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edgebound private VPC: controlplane/dataplane split + tenant ingress review (Nimbl)

Hi Danielle / Nimbl infra team,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Attached are the updated reference diagrams and a concise ingress matrix that reflect the control-plane / data-plane separation we discussed. Key points for this review: 

- Control plane (management API, certificate rotation, metrics ingestion): will originate from Redwood control plane nodes in a customer-dedicated subnet. Traffic will be allowed only to the customer-managed controlplane egress ACLs listed in the matrix.
- Data plane (inference requests): will run on tenant-dedicated compute in the on-prem cluster and use a private LB inside the customer's VPC; no public IPs for runtime nodes.
- Ingress demarcation: we recommend the customer terminate TLS at their edge LB and forward to an internal ALB with mutual TLS (mTLS) between the ALB and Redwood sidecars. The attached PDF outlines the cert rotation sequence and required subjectAltNames.

Please review the attached diagrams: 20260930-edgebound-control-data-topology-v2.drawio.png and the tenant ingress matrix. We need confirmation on the following by EOD Friday so we can finalize the runbook: 

1) Final IP ranges for the customer egress ACL (we currently show 10.240.0.0/16 plus the two peering ranges in the diagram).
2) Whether the customer will provide an internal DNS name for the mTLS endpoint or prefer Redwood manage DNS in the co-managed zone.
3) Any hard egress inspection (e.g., packet capture, IDS) that would require additional NAT traversal or port pinhole exceptions.

If it's helpful, we can run a short table-top demo next week to show the handoff and the observability hooks that surface tenant-level latency and token counts.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Attachments: 20260930-edgebound-control-data-topology-v2.drawio.png, 20260930-tenant-ingress-matrix.xlsx, 20260930-cert-rotation-and-mtls-sequence.pdf

From: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@nimblhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: infra@nimblhealth.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edgebound private VPC: controlplane/dataplane split + tenant ingress review (Nimbl)

Irene — thanks for the diagrams and the clear checklist. Quick answers from our side: 

- IP ranges: we can confirm the 10.240.0.0/16 for controlplane egress and an additional /24 (10.241.12.0/24) for the managed peering range. I attached our updated crossconnect inventory (see inline).
- DNS: we'll provide an internal FQDN under nimbl-internal.local for the mTLS endpoint; we do not want Redwood to manage DNS in our zone.
- Inspection: we will have an IDS on the perimeter. The IDS will not terminate TLS but will inspect headers/metadata via dedicated telemetry collectors. No additional NAT is expected, but we may need explicit ports opened for our telemetry agent (port 8050 TCP).

We flagged two items that need clarification: 
1) How does certificate rotation impact in-flight inference KV cache? Is there a recommended quiesce window?
2) For tenant onboarding automation, we need a variant of the ingress matrix that lists environment-specific rate limits per tenant.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow morning to walk through the cert sequence.

—Danielle
Principal Cloud Architect, Nimbl Health
Danielle.Morris@nimblhealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edgebound private VPC: controlplane/dataplane split + tenant ingress review (Nimbl)

Thanks Danielle — quick answers and a couple asks from ops: 

- Cert rotation and KV cache: our recommendation is rolling rotation per availability zone with a 30s token exchange handshake and a 2-minute soft-quiesce window for in-flight KV cache flush on the worker. That avoids a global pause; each worker will accept both old and new certs during the overlap window. I'll add sequence notes to the PDF (we should capture this in the runbook).
- Rate limits matrix: I've started a tenant rate-limits tab in the attached ingress matrix (row per tenant, columns for qps, burst, per-token cost tagging). Danielle, can you confirm the target qps per tenant for the pilot tenants?

Operationally, two items for the customer to approve: 
1) ALB healthcheck reachability: we need permission for a TCP healthcheck from Redwood probes on port 5001.
2) Observability collector egress: our metrics forwarder will push to the customer's telemetry endpoint on port 8050 (as Danielle noted). We can tunnel metrics over mTLS if preferred.

If both are approved, I'll update the runbook and cut a change window proposal.

Kimberly Park
Manager, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Edgebound private VPC: controlplane/dataplane split + tenant ingress review (Nimbl)

Adding a couple of infra-level notes from our side: 

- BGP vs static: the diagram currently assumes static routing between the on-prem leaf and the Redwood peering fabric. If Nimbl prefers BGP we can flip to a BGP session; that's slightly more operationally heavy but simplifies failover across fabric links. Please indicate preference.
- Hairpin/NAT: we need to avoid double-NAT on the inference path — the recommended pattern is hairpin at the ALB with source-preservation to allow tenant-level firewalling on Nimbl side.
- MTLS cipher suites: we'll require TLSv1.3 with AES-GCM or CHACHA20_POLY1305; please confirm any SOC2 constraints that mandate specific suites.

I'll prepare a small README for the runbook explaining the traffic flows and the expected BGP static table if you go static.

—Jonas
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — summary and agreed next steps: 

Summary of agreements
- Nimbl confirms controlplane egress 10.240.0.0/16 and peering 10.241.12.0/24.
- Nimbl will provide internal FQDN nimbl-internal.local for mTLS; Redwood will not manage DNS.
- IDS will be perimeter-only; telemetry collector will listen on port 8050.
- Cert rotation: apply rolling rotation per AZ with a 30s overlap, 2-minute soft quiesce (Kim to document).

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Danielle / Nimbl: share final crossconnect inventory and confirm pilot tenant qps by 2026-10-04 (owner: Danielle).
- Kimberly: add cert rotation sequence and tenant rate-limits tab to the ingress matrix and produce a draft runbook (owner: Kimberly) by 2026-10-02.
- Jonas: produce BGP static table example and hairpin NAT notes; include cipher suite recommendations (owner: Jonas) by 2026-10-02.
- Irene: schedule a 30-min tabletop demo for 2026-10-05; I'll send calendar invite once we have preliminary runbook.

If there are no blockers, we'll treat these approvals as sufficient to move to a staging cut next week. Danielle — say the word and we'll schedule the demo.

Best,
Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
